title: Resistor Color Code Calculator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: Pick four stripe colors to read a resistor's value in ohms, type a value to see its stripes, load common robot-lab resistors, and quiz yourself on random resistors.

learningObjectives: Read a four-band resistor's value in ohms from its stripe colors
Choose stripe colors for a target resistance value
Compute the tolerance range for a resistor
Recognize values that two digits and a multiplier cannot make exactly
prerequisites: What a resistor does in a circuit (Chapter 2: Resistors and Breadboards)

controls.label: Show stripes
controls.purpose: Set the stripes to the closest two-digit match

controls.label: Random resistor
controls.purpose: Start a quiz with the answer hidden

simulationModel.modelType: Deterministic encoding and decoding of the four-band color code
equations: range = value * (1 - tolerance) to value * (1 + tolerance)
assumptions: Four-band resistors with two significant digits
Tolerance colors limited to gold, silver and brown
limitations: Five-band and six-band precision resistors are not shown
Closest match rounds to two significant digits, not to the E12 or E24 standard series

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Worked decoding followed by retrieval practice
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Dropdown encoder/decoder with a quiz mode and example table
keyQuestions: What do the first two stripes tell you, and what does the third one do?
Why can 475 ohms not be made with a four-band resistor?
What range of real values can a 330-ohm, 5% resistor have?
commonMisconceptions: The third stripe is a third digit
The tolerance stripe changes the value
Any value can be made exactly with four stripes
assessmentOpportunities: Three correct quiz readings in a row
Exit ticket: stripes for 4.7k ohms and the range for 330 ohms at 5%
